subject: general
question:
By interchanging the given two numbers (not digits) which of the following equation will NOT be correct?

3 and 7

I. 7 × 9 + 3 - 8 ÷ 2 = 30

II. 2 × 3 + 7 - 4 ÷ 1 = 13
solution:
BODMAS Rule:

 [IMAGE: https://lh4.googleusercontent.com/c0j5U9v2oJWEzSTKvdDLWZ5Zik3PBUXk-C9w3Ma990WH63rpQUfA7g-3wh_uT7CgFvFJ4jPGEeOw509FxSgfh78_HR9tDNZ9KitXdEveKsLaLMgPQf6YSDt1b775728JMVp9FIQs=s0] 

According to the question, we need to interchange the numbers 3 and 7 and identify which of the following equations will NOT be correct.

**I. 7 × 9 + 3 - 8 ÷ 2 = 30**

New Equation: 3 × 9 + 7 - 8 ÷ 2 = ?

Perform operations according to BODMAS:

⇒ 3 × 9 + 7 - (__**8 ÷ 2**__)

⇒ (__**3 × 9**__) + 7 - 4

⇒ (__**27 + 7**__) - 4

⇒ __**34 - 4**__

⇒ 30

30 = 30 (Equation I is Correct)

**II. 2 × 3 + 7 - 4 ÷ 1 = 13**

New Equation: 2 × 7 + 3 - 4 ÷ 1 = ?

Perform operations according to BODMAS:

⇒ 2 × 7 + 3 - (__**4 ÷ 1**__)

⇒ (__**2 × 7**__) + 3 - 4

⇒ (__**14 + 3**__) - 4

⇒ __**17 - 4**__

⇒ 13

13 = 13 (Equation II is Correct)

Since both equations I and II are correct after the interchange, neither of them is "not correct".

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".
